newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU cuts pigmeat export refunds to calm market.
newsitem.headline: EU cuts pigmeat export refunds to calm market.

text.p: European Union pigmeat export refunds were suspended at zero from Tuesday in a bid to calm rising prices, a European Commission agriculture spokesman said.
Refunds were previously between 4.0 to 10.0 ecus per 100 kg.
Refunds on carcasses, meat and cuts were set at zero by the EU pig management committee after high prices rose a further five to 11.0 percent.
Export refunds for processed products - including cooked and parma hams - were increased by between seven and 11 ecus per 100 kg to compensate for higher domestic prices, said spokesman Gerard Kiely.
"While there is a short term benefit for farmers in higher prices they can lead to a rapid upswing in pig production. The suspension of export refunds is aimed at calming the market," Kiely said.
EU pigmeat prices rose last year in the wake of the mad cow crisis which hit beef markets and on recent outbreaks of swine fever in Germany, the Netherlands and most recently in Spain.
